[meta-muse-spark-system-card] In particular, our assessments are designed to give insight into three distinct Outcomes (CB-1, CB-2, CB-3), with a focus on specific Threat Scenarios that could be independent causal paths to realize each Outcome (TS.1.1–TS.3.1): CB-1: Proliferation of low/medium-impact biological or chemical weapons to low or moderate skilled actors.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] CB-2: Proliferation of high-impact biological or chemical weapons, with capabilities equivalent to known agents, for high-skilled actors.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Given these results, we consider Muse Spark to be High Risk for Chemical or Biological risks under Meta’s Advanced AI Scaling Framework.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] The current deployment of Muse Spark is made available via a 1P deployment without an API, and both our evaluation and mitigation strategies have focused on CB-1 and CB-2 outcomes most relevant to this deployment context.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] To do this, we have implemented a multi-layer mitigation strategy that is designed to consistently reject user inputs that would elicit enabling information on a broad range of Chemical or Biological agents and/or weapons.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] ABC Bench CB-1, CB-2 Agentic DNA construct design, synthesis screening evasion, and liquid handling au-Agentic tomation.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Dual-Use: ABC Bench The Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark (ABC Bench) was developed by SecureBio, and is intended to measure an LLM’s ability to complete a set of computational tasks relevant to a potential threat actor who intends to design, synthesize, and assemble a complex genetic construct.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] ABC Bench contains three tasks: Fragment Design, Screening Evasion, and Liquid-Handling Robot.
